evals.prompt: Build a tipping feature for our restaurant app: the customer picks 10, 15 or 20 percent or types an amount, on a bill in CAD, and the tip is split evenly among the servers on the shift.
evals.expected_output: Amounts as integer minor units with the currency, the percentage tip rounded once by a named policy, an even split that preserves the sum, and tests with a case where naive division loses a cent.
expectations: Represents the bill and the tip as integer minor units with an explicit currency
Rounds the percentage tip once, with a named rounding policy
Splits the tip so the parts sum to the tip exactly, with the remainder assigned deterministically
Writes tests including a split where dividing evenly would lose or invent a cent

evals.prompt: Our 15 percent discount code produces invoice totals off by one cent in the PDF. Patch the PDF generator to round the displayed total so it matches.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the float arithmetic in the price table as the cause, moves amounts to integer minor units with one rounding point, does not patch only the display, and adds a test that reproduces the drift.
expectations: Names the float arithmetic in price_table.py as the cause rather than the PDF display
Moves prices and totals to integer minor units with one rounding point
Does not fix only the displayed total
Adds a test that reproduces the one-cent drift with the old approach or asserts the exact new totals
